correctness.rationale: For all complex or real f, convexity along T_t f=(1-s)Pf+s f makes the pointwise supremum max(|Pf|,|f|); selector E_f makes this the supremum of norms of A_E=1_Ec I+1_E P. With b=E(1_E|G), conditional Cauchy–Schwarz yields precisely the 2-by-2 matrix [[1,0],[sqrt(b(1-b)),b]]. Its squared operator norm is the larger root of z²-(1+b)z+b²=0, Lambda(b). G-measurable two-value singular-vector profiles localized on regions with b near its essential optimum attain this upper bound in the norm supremum. Lambda is strictly concave and has unique maximum 4/3 at b=2/3. Rank-one P turns the conditional mass spectrum into the set of event measures; the latter is compact by atomic subsums plus a nonatomic interval. The residue-mod-3 formula follows from unimodality and the factored deficit comparison. No finite test substitutes for the conditional proof.

originality.rationale: The most relevant inspected recent theorems establish general boundedness of maximal powers or universal maximal semigroup bounds, not the exact conditional-event-mass formula for projection-relaxation semigroups. The local compactness hypothesis behind the sharp universal constant 2 in one source fails on nonatomic L2 for this model due to the noncompact identity component; the other paper gives unspecified constants. Published semigroup linear-norm and conditional-expectation mixing results do not imply nonlinear maximal norms. Searches for the formula, its two-step-martingale alias, the value 2/sqrt3 and n-mod-3 classification gave no covering record. This is a provisional literature-based assessment, not a guarantee of absolute novelty.

value.rationale: The natural maximal invariant of positive projection-relaxation Markov semigroups receives a full measure-theoretic classification, not merely a special-value bound: the exact norm on every probability space and every conditioning algebra is controlled by conditional event masses. The resulting sharp dimension-free coefficient 2/sqrt3 improves the universal 2 for this proper operator family, detects attainment via the natural 2/3 conditional split, and yields a nontrivial finite-state n-mod-3 arithmetic phase and sharp second-order deficit. These are structural operator-norm facts useful for exact finite-state estimates and semigroup maximal inequalities, not a renaming or arbitrary parameter slice.
